ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The large square in the figure is divided into four equal large square regions. The upper-right large square is white, the lower-left large square is white, and the lower-right large square is entirely colored gray. The upper-left large square is further divided into a 3×3 small grid, in which the top two rows, totaling 6 small squares, are all gray, and the third row has 2 white small squares and 1 gray small square, so the upper-left region has a total of 7 gray small squares and 2 white small squares. Reasoning: The lower-right large square accounts for 1/4 of the entire large square, and is entirely gray. The upper-left large square also accounts for 1/4 of the whole, of which the gray part accounts for 7/9, so the gray area it contributes is (7/9)×(1/4)=7/36. The total gray area proportion is 1/4+7/36=9/36+7/36=16/36=4/9.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a large square split into four equal large squares. From the image, the bottom-right large square is entirely grey, the top-right and bottom-left large squares are white, and the top-left large square is further split into a 3 by 3 grid. In that top-left 3 by 3 grid, count 7 grey small squares and 2 white small squares. Since the top-left large square is one fourth of the whole, its grey contribution is (7/9)(1/4), and the bottom-right grey square contributes 1/4. Add these areas: 1/4 + 7/36 = 16/36 = 4/9.
